acceptance_criteria: Per-user routing contract added. Patch routing tests pass.
close_reason: Added is_per_user_property and update_task_per_user (default delegates to update_object) to TasksBackend; handler routes per-user-only patches to update_task_per_user; 3 new routing tests; 22 total pass; clippy clean
description:
**What:** Draft-tasks-06 §4.5.1 defines per-user properties for Task: keywords, color, freeBusyStatus, useDefaultAlerts, alerts. The handler must route patches containing only per-user properties to a separate update path.

**Algorithm:**
1. Add static method to TasksBackend:
   fn is_per_user_property(prop: &str) -> bool {
       matches!(prop, "keywords" | "color" | "freeBusyStatus" | "useDefaultAlerts" | "alerts")
   }
2. Add to TasksBackend:
   fn update_task_per_user(&self, account_id: &Id, id: &Id, patch: Value) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Option<Task>, BackendSetError<Self::Error>>> + Send;
   Default impl: delegates to update_object::<Task>(account_id, id, patch).
3. In handle_task_set update loop: inspect top-level patch keys. If ALL non-null keys are per-user properties → call update_task_per_user. Otherwise → call update_object as before.
4. Document: when only per-user properties are patched, the shared 'updated' timestamp must NOT change (§4.5.1 lines 978-981). The default impl is correct only for single-user scenarios.

**Tests:**
- Patch {"color":"#ff0000"} → update_task_per_user called with that patch.
- Patch {"title":"New"} → update_object called.
- Patch {"color":"#ff","title":"New"} → update_object called (mixed).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Default impl compiles and passes all existing tests.
- cargo test -p jmap-tasks-server exits 0.
title: Add per-user property routing contract to TasksBackend
